title: Signals, memos, and guarded routes
summary: Build a shared cart store with signals, a memoized total, and a route guard.

scenario.briefing: The cart recalculates its total in a plain function and never blocks checkout when it is empty. Build a shared signal store, memoize the total, and guard the route.

objectives.description: Apply the taught syntax in a working file.
Review an artifact and identify the concrete risks.

hints: Create the signal with createSignal and read it by calling items().
Wrap the store factory in createRoot so its memo has an owner.
Derive the total with createMemo instead of a plain function.
In the route guard, throw redirect("/catalog") when the cart is empty.

misconceptions.description: Deriving state in a plain function instead of a memo.
misconceptions.feedback: A plain function recomputes on every call and has no reactive owner. createMemo caches the value and tracks its dependencies.
misconceptions.testDescription: The store uses a shared signal and a memoized total.

misconceptions.feedback: Use <For each={items()}> so Solid reconciles rows by identity and tracks the source.
misconceptions.diagnostic: Rendering with map rebuilds rows and loses the For component's identity tracking.

misconceptions.description: Shipping a list built with map instead of For.
misconceptions.feedback: Map rebuilds every row and loses identity. Block the change until the list uses For with a stable key.

sections.title: Signals are the source of truth
sections.body: createSignal returns a getter and a setter. Components read the getter inside JSX, and Solid subscribes only those expressions to changes.

sections.title: Memos derive values
sections.body: createMemo caches a computation and recomputes it when a dependency changes. A plain function has no owner and no cache, so it cannot act as derived state.

sections.title: Lists and branches use control flow
sections.body: Render reactive lists with <For each={items()}> and conditionals with <Show>. Map rebuilds rows on every change, while For reconciles them by item identity.

sections.title: Guards run before the route
sections.body: A router beforeLoad guard can throw redirect to send the user elsewhere before the destination renders.

steps.title: Build the shared cart store
steps.prompt: Edit cart.ts. Create the shared store with createSignal, derive the total with createMemo, update items immutably, and redirect empty carts to the catalog.

tests.description: The store uses a shared signal and a memoized total.
Adding an item updates the signal immutably.
The route guard redirects an empty cart to the catalog.

hints: Create a shared signal with createSignal and a store factory wrapped in createRoot.
Read the signal by calling items(), not by reading items.value.
Derive total with createMemo so it recomputes only when items change.
Throw redirect("/catalog") from the guard when the cart is empty.

artifact.caption: The component destructures props and renders rows with map instead of For.

findings.label: Destructuring props captures the current products array instead of reading the live prop.
The list renders with map instead of For, so rows are rebuilt rather than reconciled by item identity.
The list already uses For to reconcile rows by identity.

verdicts.label: Block the change until props are read live and the list uses For.
Ship it; map renders the same rows.
Only the input markup needs work.

steps.explanation: Destructuring props snapshots the initial array, so later parent updates never reach this component. Rendering with map instead of <For each={props.products}> rebuilds every row instead of reconciling by item identity.
hints: Check whether the total is derived or recalculated in a plain function.
Look for list rendering that recreates every row.
Check the guard for a deny path when the cart is empty.
Block only for findings that are present in the artifact.
